Favor exposure to digital infrastructure and fintech plays, given the structural tailwinds from rising internet penetration and regulatory support for cashless payments.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export demand remains structurally supported by Asian power generation needs, with domestic players like BAJA and INDY benefiting from stable pricing and local offtake agreements.
Nickel downstreaming policies in Indonesia continue to drive value-add processing, favoring companies like ALKA and GDST that integrate smelting capacity.
US interest rate sensitivity creates divergence: ID-listed miners outperform as rupiah stability aids margins, while US-exposed names like BHP face cost pressure from stronger dollar.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's mining & energy sector shows resilience with domestic names like BAJA (+34.55%) and ALKA (+25.00%) surging, while US-listed peers lag. Focus on coal and nickel plays as global demand shifts; INDY and BKR gains signal local strength. Maintain overweight on ID-listed miners, but watch for US macro headwinds that could pressure BHP and SHW.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Geothermal expansion remains a durable driver as Indonesia targets 7.2 GW by 2030, with PGEO leading development under favorable regulatory frameworks and state-backed financing.
EV battery supply chain integration, supported by nickel downstreaming policies, creates structural demand for VKTR and related component makers despite near-term price volatility.
US climate-tech names like ENPH and ARRY benefit from IRA incentives and grid modernization trends, offering diversification against Indonesia-specific political and currency risks.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector shows a WATCH signal with selective strength in VKTR and PGEO, but aggregate weakness suggests near-term caution. Focus on EV and geothermal plays as policy catalysts emerge, while US-listed names like ARRY and ENPH offer relative resilience. Position for a Q2 recovery in domestic names tied to the new capital and energy transition mandates.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's rising middle class and urbanization continue to drive steady demand for essential consumer goods and packaged foods, supporting FMCG volume growth.
Government infrastructure spending and minimum wage hikes are boosting rural purchasing power, expanding the addressable market for mass-market consumer staples.
Digitalization of retail and direct-to-consumer channels is enabling faster inventory turnover and margin expansion for agile FMCG players with strong e-commerce integration.
sectors.ai: Watch consumer/FMCG selectively: AGAR, ZONE, WOOD, SMLE, ECII, GRPM, BTEK, MPPA surged 8–25% on rotational demand and resilient domestic spending. Favor names with strong distribution and pricing power; avoid chasing momentum without earnings confirmation.
